newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's 1998 poll should be on EMU - Centre Party.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's 1998 poll should be on EMU - Centre Party.

text.p: Sweden's Centre Party, the ruling Social Democrats' informal coalition partner, said on Tuesday the next scheduled general election in 1998 should be used to determine if Sweden should join Europe's economic and monetary union.

"There is a particular need to make the 1998 elections into a poll on EMU since part of what Prime Minister (Goran Persson) is saying opens the door to a new decision on EMU already in the next mandate period," Centre Party leader Olof Johansson said.
In the ruling Social Democrat party's first public announcement, Persson said Sweden would join EMU when it was possible and that it was not closing the door completely.
"Our decision not to join does not apply indefinitely in the future. There can be a situation in the next mandate period (1998-2002) when we would attempt to join," Persson said.
"I was hoping he (Persson) would have said 2002," Johansson told reporters.
The Centre Party said it stood by its view and was still against Sweden joining EMU.
"We are saying no to EMU for the foreseeable future," Johansson said.
He said that the Centre Party's relationship with the Social Democrats would change ahead of the 1998 elections.
However Johansson said there would be no change in the short term to its cooperation with the party.
"The sorting out of state finances is for the most part completed. Now it's important to make sure we stick to the decisions," Johansson said.
